architecture.mechanism: More-electric and electronic control algorithms with cascade and advanced control strategies for engine operability and fault-tolerant performance management
architecture.intervention: Apply a fault-tolerant more-electric/electronic engine control architecture to the Subaru Outback that uses redundant electrical power pathways and cascade control logic to maintain ECU operation and instrument panel power when the primary bus faults, isolating the stall trigger by supervising battery and alternator state in real time.
architecture.expected_effect: Elimination of simultaneous engine stall and instrument panel blackout at 12,500 miles by ensuring that a detected electrical fault triggers controlled power re-routing rather than total loss of ECU and gauge cluster power.
architecture.falsification_test: On a bench-rig replicating the 2021 Outback charging/bus topology, inject the documented failure mode (battery/alternator bus interruption) with and without the cascade more-electric supervisory controller installed; the intervention passes only if the ECU remains energized and the instrument panel retains illumination throughout the simulated stall event.
